newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK RATES SPIKE, BONDS FALL ON LIQUIDITY SQUEEZE.
newsitem.headline: GREEK RATES SPIKE, BONDS FALL ON LIQUIDITY SQUEEZE.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards were up 20 to 50 basis points after mid-session pushing fixed coupon bonds lower and dealers blamed it on an emerging liquidity squeeze in the local market.
Ecu/drachma was fluctuating in the 309.0/50 corridor in quiet dealings, dealers said.

"Depos and forex forwards have risen 20 to 50 basis points on what appears to be a liquidity squeeze," said a dealer. "There is an auction of seven-year FRNs on June 26 and the state is to collect the proceeds from OTE's part-float starting Monday."
The finance ministry will auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year FRNs on June 26. Telecom OTE raised about 340 billion drachmas from local and foreign investors in its recent part-flotation.

"The local market is short drachmas but London is long drachmas and basically sets tomnext rates from forex forwards," said a trader at a foreign bank. "Forex forwards just follow depos and they are also up."
Higher interbank rates were putting downward pressure on fixed coupon bonds. Seven-year and 10-year bonds were hit harder shedding 30 to 40 basis points, bond dealers said.

"Seven- and 10-year bonds have lost 30 to 40 basis points while three-year bonds have suffered smaller losses and FRNs are steady," said a bond dealer at a private bank. "Higher interbank rates account for the losses."
The mark was quoted at 158.02/07 from Thursday's 158.090 fix, the dollar at 272.85/95 drachmas from 273.660 and the ecu at 309.25/35 from 309.380 drachmas.

"The forex market is quiet and ecu/drachma is ranging," said a dealer. "The official exchange rate policy is known to the market which is convinced that the anti-inflationary, hard drachma policy is here to stay and higher rates just provide a comfortable support for the drachma."
